questions.question: In the simplex algorithm for $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form, the reduced cost $\bar{c}_j$ of a nonbasic $x_j$ is its objective-row entry, and $\bar{c}_j<0$ means that raising $x_j$ increases $Z$. Which nonbasic variable enters under Bland's rule?
options: The one with the most negative $\bar{c}_j$, ties going to the smallest $j$
The one with the smallest index $j$ among those with $\bar{c}_j<0$
The one with the smallest index $j$ among all nonbasic variables
The one with the smallest index $j$ among those with $\bar{c}_j>0$

questions.question: Bland's theorem concerns the (revised) simplex algorithm, run with Bland's rule on a linear program in equation form. Which statement does the theorem guarantee?
options: No basis is visited twice, so the algorithm stops after finitely many iterations
It never needs more iterations than the rule with the most negative reduced cost
It cannot cycle, but only on linear programs without degenerate corner points
It ends with an optimal solution whenever the linear program is feasible

questions.question: In a simplex tableau of a maximization in equation form, $x_{j^*}$ enters. The ordinary minimum-ratio test lets any row attaining the minimum ratio leave. In which situation does the leaving part of Bland's rule actually restrict this choice?
options: Whenever the minimum ratio is $0$, that is, at every degenerate step of the algorithm
Whenever two or more rows have a positive entry in the entering column of $x_{j^*}$
Only when two or more rows with a positive entry in the entering column attain the minimum ratio
Whenever $x_{j^*}$ was not the nonbasic variable with the most negative reduced cost

questions.question: Bland's rule is added to the simplex algorithm for $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form, either in tableau form or as the revised simplex algorithm. Which statement about what it changes is correct?
options: The minimum-ratio test is replaced: the basic variable with the smallest index always leaves
Only the choice of entering and of tied leaving variables; the stopping test and the ratio test stay
It works only in tableau form, because the revised simplex algorithm has no rows to compare
The stopping test changes: stop once the nonbasic variable of smallest index has $\bar{c}_j\geq0$

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form, a feasible tableau has basic variables $x_1,x_4,x_7$ and objective row $Z+2x_2-x_3-3x_5+4x_6=15$ (reduced costs are the objective-row entries; a negative one means $Z$ can increase). Which variable enters under Bland's rule?

For a maximization in equation form, $x_2$ enters a feasible tableau. From the top row down, the rows are (basic variable: right-hand side, entry in the $x_2$ column) $x_6\colon2,\,1$; $x_3\colon6,\,3$; $x_1\colon9,\,3$; $x_5\colon1,\,\tfrac{1}{4}$. Which variable leaves under Bland's rule?

A linear program has structural variables $x_1,\dots,x_4$ and two constraints, with slack variables numbered after the structural ones. A feasible tableau of $\max Z$ has basic variables $x_2,x_4$ and reduced costs (objective-row entries) $\bar{c}_1=0$, $\bar{c}_3=-\tfrac{1}{2}$, $-1$ for the slack of constraint 1 and $-3$ for the slack of constraint 2. Which variable enters under Bland's rule?
options: The slack variable of constraint 1
The slack variable of constraint 2
The structural variable $x_1$
The structural variable $x_3$

questions.question: In the proof of Bland's theorem, a variable is fickle if it is basic in some but not all bases of a cycle, and $l$ is the largest fickle index. A run on a linear program with variables $x_1,\dots,x_8$ and three equations cycles through the six bases $\{x_1,x_2,x_6\}$, $\{x_3,x_2,x_6\}$, $\{x_3,x_4,x_6\}$, $\{x_5,x_4,x_6\}$, $\{x_5,x_7,x_6\}$, $\{x_1,x_7,x_6\}$ and back. What is $l$?

For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form, a feasible tableau has basic variables $x_2=3$, $x_5=1$, objective row $Z-x_1+2x_3-5x_4=7$ (reduced costs are the objective-row entries; a negative one means $Z$ can increase), and rows $x_2-2x_1+x_3+x_4=3$, $x_5-x_1-x_3+3x_4=1$. What happens in the next step under Bland's rule?
options: $x_1$ has no finite ratio and is skipped; $x_4$ enters and $x_5$ leaves
$x_1$ enters and $x_2$ leaves, as the basic variable with the smallest index
$x_1$ enters; no row limits its increase, so $Z$ is unbounded
$x_1$ cannot be increased, so no variable enters and the tableau is optimal

questions.question: Bland's rule guarantees that the simplex algorithm on a linear program in equation form with $m$ equations and $m+n$ variables never visits a basis twice. What else does the argument that the algorithm stops need?
options: That the feasible region of the linear program is bounded
That ties in the minimum-ratio test never occur during the run
That the linear program has an optimal solution to converge to
That there are only finitely many bases, at most $\binom{m+n}{m}$

questions.question: Let $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ have an optimal solution. A proof of strong duality runs the simplex algorithm from a feasible corner point and takes $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ in the final tableau. What does Bland's rule add?
options: It guarantees a final tableau without negative reduced costs, so that $\boldsymbol{y}$ is dual feasible
It makes the optimal solution unique, so that the dual solution read off the final tableau is well defined
It avoids degenerate steps, since a degenerate final tableau gives no dual feasible $\boldsymbol{y}$
Nothing essential: every simplex run stops after finitely many steps, and Bland's rule only shortens it

questions.question: With Bland's rule, the simplex algorithm for a maximization reaches a degenerate feasible corner point $\boldsymbol{x}^0$, and the current basis still has a negative reduced cost. Which statement about the continuation is correct?
options: Its next basis change moves to an adjacent corner point with a strictly larger $Z$
It may change bases at $\boldsymbol{x}^0$ forever, but it never repeats any basis
After finitely many basis changes it moves to a corner point with larger $Z$ or stops
It stops at $\boldsymbol{x}^0$, since at a degenerate corner point $Z$ cannot increase

questions.question: For $\max Z=3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq4$, $x_1\leq3$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $x_3,x_4$, Ana and Ben both start from the slack basis at $(0,0)$ and apply Bland's rule. Ben has swapped the names of $x_1$ and $x_2$ beforehand, so his smallest index belongs to the original $x_2$. Which statement is correct?
options: Both first reach $(3,0)$, as swapping names changes no reduced cost; both runs stop
Ana first reaches $(3,0)$ and Ben $(0,4)$; both runs are guaranteed to stop
Ana first reaches $(3,0)$ and Ben $(0,4)$; only Ana's run is guaranteed to stop
Ana first reaches $(3,0)$ and Ben $(0,4)$; they stop at different optimal points

questions.question: In a degenerate feasible tableau of a maximization in equation form, $x_3$ is the entering variable. Its column has entries $2$, $-2$, $\tfrac{1}{3}$, $\tfrac{1}{4}$ in the rows of the basic variables $x_6$, $x_1$, $x_4$, $x_2$, whose right-hand sides are $0$, $0$, $0$, $1$. Which basic variable does Bland's rule remove from the basis?

For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form, a feasible tableau has basic variables $x_1=6$, $x_3=4$, objective row $Z-x_2-4x_4+2x_5=10$ (reduced costs are the objective-row entries; a negative one means $Z$ can increase), and rows $x_1+2x_2+x_4+x_5=6$, $x_3+x_2+2x_4-x_5=4$. What is $Z$ after one iteration with Bland's rule?

Bland's theorem is proved by contradiction. Assume the simplex algorithm with Bland's rule cycles, let $x_l$ have the largest index among variables basic in some but not all bases of the cycle, and compare the step where $x_l$ leaves with a later step where it enters again. Which statement about the proof is correct?
options: Only the entering part is used, because ties in the minimum-ratio test cannot occur within a cycle
Only the leaving part is used, because the entering variables of a cycle all have reduced cost $0$
Both parts of Bland's rule are used: the entering part controls reduced costs, the leaving part the direction
Neither part is used: the contradiction is that $Z$ strictly increases from one basis to the next

questions.question: Consider $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with a known basis of a feasible corner point, and suppose $Z$ is bounded above on the feasible region. What does the simplex algorithm with Bland's rule show about this linear program?
options: It has an optimal solution only if its feasible region is bounded as well as its objective
It has an optimal solution, and that solution is unique: the corner point where the run stops
It has an optimal solution only if it has no degenerate corner point, as it might cycle otherwise
It has an optimal solution at a feasible corner point, even if its feasible region is unbounded

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ in equation form, a feasible tableau has basic variables $x_5$ (top row) and $x_3$ (second row), objective row $Z+x_1-2x_2-x_4=0$ (reduced costs are the objective-row entries; a negative one means $Z$ can increase), and rows $x_5-3x_1+x_2+x_4=0$, $x_3-2x_1+2x_2-2x_4=0$. How does the simplex algorithm with Bland's rule continue?
options: $x_2$ replaces $x_5$; $x_1$ replaces $x_3$; then $x_4$ enters without a positive entry
$x_2$ replaces $x_3$; then $x_1$ enters with no positive column entry, so $Z$ is unbounded
$x_2$ replaces $x_3$; then $x_4$ replaces $x_5$, and the algorithm continues at $Z=0$
$x_1$ enters at once; its column has no positive entry, so $Z$ is unbounded right away

questions.question: Consider $\max Z=2x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_2\leq2$, $x_1+2x_2\leq6$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $x_3,x_4$, from the slack basis at $(0,0)$. How many iterations (basis changes) until the optimal tableau does each entering rule need?
options: One with Bland's rule, three with the most negative reduced cost
Two with Bland's rule, four with the most negative reduced cost
One with Bland's rule, two with the most negative reduced cost
Three with Bland's rule, only one with the most negative reduced cost
